turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on at, on and in for time?
turns.tutor:
The rule: use at with clock times, on with days and dates, in with months and years.
Right: "The film starts at six o'clock."
Wrong: "The film starts in six o'clock." The time word is a clock time, so in is the wrong word.
I think aloud: "The zoo is closed on Saturday."
First, I find the time word: Saturday.
Next, I ask: clock time, day or month? It is a day.
So I use on.
Your turn. Write in, on or at:
My train leaves ___ 5 o'clock.
